blockers.title: Generation collapse NOT fixed — fm + LR isolation only DELAYED it (ep5 -> ep18, same endpoint)

comparison_baseline.note: the fm=false baseline ends at essentially the SAME 0.062, so the fm objective did not change the endpoint — it moved the onset from epoch ~5 to epoch ~18.

metric.confound_warning: That baseline ran BEFORE the LR-isolation fix (16:36 vs fix at 20:33), so it differs in TWO variables. A clean single-variable control (fm=false on the fixed trainer) is running as cfm_fm_control_2026_10_09 and is the only valid comparison; the pre-16:36 baseline is a historical reference only.

CLEAN_AB_2026_10_10.design: single variable (use_fm_objective), both arms on the LR-isolation-fixed trainer, 30 epochs, identical config otherwise

collapse_onset_epoch.note: same onset; fm=false then collapses to a HARD ZERO at ep21 and stays there for 10 epochs, fm=true bottoms at 0.0625

CLEAN_AB_2026_10_10.VERDICT: Pareto trade-off, cleanly measured. The flow-matching objective does NOT prevent the collapse — both arms collapse from the same epoch. It roughly DOUBLES residual generation capability (decode_ratio 0.583 vs 0.250; gen_validity 0.063 vs 0.000) at the cost of the bond head (0.670 vs 0.784, delta -0.113).
CLEAN_AB_2026_10_10.BOND F1 IS A NEW PROJECT RECORD: fm=false reached 0.7836 vs the previous best 0.481 (+63% relative). The gain is real and is the single largest metric movement today — but it was bought with total generation failure, so it is NOT a free win and must not be reported alone.

root_cause: The collapse is a multi-task trade-off, not a single missing lever. With the bond head unfrozen the bond CE term dominates the loss by magnitude and the optimiser wins at that objective while generation degrades.

MEASURED loss composition (42-step CPU probe of the exact config): bond_ce 1.82 -> 95% of the live loss; wasserstein 4.3-4.9%; entropy_term 0.76-0.85%; 0.05*cb_loss 0.35-0.41%; the other 8 of 12 registered terms are exact zeros.

LITERATURE (UniGEM, arXiv 2410.10516): training generation and prediction jointly 'significantly degrades the performance of both tasks'. Their fix is to activate the predictive head only in LATER diffusion stages, after structure has formed. Our bond head is active across the entire trajectory.

LITERATURE (Dey & Ning, J. Cheminformatics 2024): auxiliary-task gradients can be orders of magnitude larger than the target gradient and crowd the objective out. Our bond_ce/bond_ce ratio is the measured instance.

MEASURED 2026-10-10 (clean A/B): the flow-matching objective is a MITIGATION, not a cure. Collapse onset is identical (ep18) in both arms, so the absence of fm_term is not the cause — BLK-C12 (bond_ce at ~95% of the loss) is. FM buys about 2.3x residual decode capability and costs 0.113 bond F1.
fix_steps: Step 1: Wait for cfm_fm_control_2026_10_09 and read the single-variable fm delta before attributing anything.
Step 2: Implement UniGEM's late-stage activation — gate the bond head's contribution by diffusion timestep so it only shapes the late (structure-formed) part of the trajectory.
Step 3: If that is too invasive, the cheaper test is to train the bond head as a separate stage or with a much smaller weight, and check whether generation recovers.
Step 4: Turn on pcgrad_multi_task (the flag exists, default false) so conflicting gradients are projected rather than summed — PCGrad, arXiv:2001.06782.

Step 5: Re-measure the FULL 30-epoch curve. Do NOT read a mid-run checkpoint: this run read 0.5391 bond_f1 at epoch 15, which sits just before the collapse and would have supported exactly the wrong conclusion.
blockers.smoke_gate: §5.7 50-step CPU; assert the bond term's gradient actually reaches the shared backbone (grad norm > 0) and that decode_ratio > 0
blockers.honest_negative_fallback: If late-stage activation does not recover generation, the bond head and the generator are architecturally in conflict in this setup. Report as such rather than continuing to tune weights.

metric_confound_found_2026_10_10.mechanism: 两臂 recall 都 ~0.89-0.92 而 exact_match 皆 0 —— bond head 塌向'对每个候选对都预测有键'。全正基线在 pos_rate 0.2986 下 F1≈0.460。F1 高低实际由 precision 决定，而 precision 跟着生成能力走：生成一死 F1 就涨。fm=false 的训练器自己写下 'gen_validity is saturated at 0.000 over n=48 samples: it carries no gradient this run'。

blockers.title: The loss contains no generation objective at all — 8 of 12 terms are exact zeros

MEASURED.source: 42-step CPU probe of configs/cfm_blk_c5_repair_2026_10_09.yaml reading the trainer's own _LAST_LOSS_TERMS

root_cause: Whatever the bond head is doing, nothing in the loss is asking the model to GENERATE well. The sampler is steered entirely by the bond CE it was trained on.

The fragments the sampler actually emits (MEASURED, 609 rows from cfm_fm_ab_2026_10_09/generated_smiles.csv): 64.9% multi-fragment, 44.7% contain a 1-atom fragment, and only 63.4% are unique. The pre-16:36 baseline was 100% unique. Uniqueness DEGRADED during training.
The pathology is degenerate fragmentation into loose atoms, not the hypervalent garbage previously assumed: ZERO valence violations across the whole set (max explicit valence 6, no C>4).
generated_smiles.csv is append-gated on _decode_with_rdkit_strict, so it contains only parseable survivors — unparseable failures are structurally invisible there.
fix_steps: Step 1: Decide what the generation objective IS. Candidates: uniqueness/diversity, fragment-count penalty, valency-consistency on the decoded graph, or a reconstruction term.

Step 2: Note that a pure RDKit valency penalty would repeat the BLK-C5 mistake — it is non-differentiable. It must be a differentiable proxy over the graph the sampler emits, or applied at sampling time.
Step 3: Track uniqueness as a first-class metric. It is the one that moved the wrong way and it is not currently reported.

literature_2026_10_10.why: The 2026-10-09/10 CFM work measured a multi-task trade-off, not a missing knob. These are the papers that say what to do about that specifically. Nothing here has been read in full — they are leads selected from search, to be read before any of the above is implemented.

entries.paper: UniGEM: A Unified Approach to Generation and Property Prediction for Molecules
entries.why: Closest match to what we measured. Reports that joint generation + prediction training 'significantly degrades the performance of both tasks', and attributes it to the denoiser being active across the whole trajectory while properties are only meaningful once structure has formed. Fix: activate the predictive head only in later diffusion stages.

entries.paper: Your Discrete Graph Diffusion Model is Secretly Memorizing
entries.why: CONDITIONAL MEMORISATION in graph diffusion coincides with a growing generalisation gap, and CANNOT be mitigated by early stopping. Memorisation onset always precedes structure emergence, so earlier checkpoints give structureless graphs. Directly relevant: our gen_validity peaks at epoch 7-13 then falls to 0.0625 — if this mechanism is ours, early stopping the run at its best gen_validity would be the wrong move, and we should NOT reach for it without reading this first.

entries.paper: Bigger Isn't Always Memorizing: Early Stopping Overparameterized Diffusion Models
entries.why: Generalisation is achieved BEFORE memorisation onset, and memorisation time scales linearly with dataset size. Demonstrated on D3PM, the discrete-diffusion family graph models use. Gives a quantitative handle on WHERE in an epoch curve quality should peak — relevant because our curve peaks at ep7-13 of 30.

entries.paper: PCGrad: Gradient Surgery for Multi-Task Learning
entries.why: We ALREADY HAVE the flag: configs/cfm_blk_c5_repair sets pcgrad_multi_task: false. Projecting conflicting gradients is the standard remedy for exactly the bond-CE-dominates situation we measured, and it is currently switched off.

entries.paper: Enhancing molecular property prediction with auxiliary learning and task-specific adaptation
entries.why: Auxiliary-task gradients can be orders of magnitude larger than the target gradient and crowd the objective out. Our bond_ce/bond_ce ratio of ~95% is the measured instance.

entries.paper: MolDiff: Addressing the Atom-Bond Inconsistency Problem in 3D Molecule Diffusion Generation
entries.why: Joint atom-bond generation beats post-hoc bond inference; validity improves ~3x. Relevant to how our YuelBond bond head relates to the sampler.

entries.paper: Do Graph Diffusion Models Accurately Capture and Generate Substructure Distributions?
entries.why: GDM scores well on validity while showing TV distance ~1.0 on 7-node paths and 6-node cycles — i.e. VALIDITY IS A WEAK PROXY, exactly as decode_ratio=1.000 coexisting with 64.9% fragmentation showed for us. Also identifies the GNN backbone's subgraph-counting expressivity as a bottleneck.

entries.paper: How Far Can You Grow? Characterizing the Extrapolation Frontier of Graph Generative Models for Materials Science
entries.why: Local bond fidelity diverges wildly OOD (BondMAE up to 2.09x) while global geometry stays plausible — a warning that our plausible-looking molecules may hide local chemical damage.

entries.paper: Curriculum Sampling: A Two-Phase Curriculum for Efficient Training of Flow Matching
entries.why: Middle-biased timestep sampling accelerates early convergence but imposes an asymptotic quality ceiling; documents a U-shaped per-timestep loss profile. Evaluated on images, not molecules — treat as a lead, not evidence.
